abs.description: Computes the absolute value of each element in a vector register. The most negative integer has no positive counterpart: its absolute value is itself (`-128` in `int8`).

acos.description: Computes the arc cosine of each floating-point element in radians.

acosh.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic cosine of each floating-point element.

add.description: Adds two vector registers element-wise. The integer additions wrap around (modulo $2^n$: `100 + 100` is `-56` in `int8`); `adds` saturates instead.

adds.description: Adds two integer vector registers element-wise with saturation to [MIN, MAX] on underflow/overflow.

all.description: Tests if every element of a mask register is active (returns 1 if all active, 0 otherwise).

andb.description: Computes the bitwise AND of two vector registers.

andb_k.description: Computes the bitwise AND of two mask registers.

andnb.description: Computes the bitwise AND-NOT of two vector registers (`~a & b`).

andnb_k.description: Computes the bitwise AND-NOT of two mask registers (~`vm0` & `vm1`).

any.description: Tests if at least one element of a mask register is active (returns 1 if any active, 0 otherwise).

asin.description: Computes the arc sine of each floating-point element in radians.

asinh.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic sine of each floating-point element.

atan.description: Computes the arc tangent of each floating-point element in radians.

atan2.description: Computes the four-quadrant arc tangent of y and x floating-point vector elements.

atanh.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic tangent of each floating-point element.

bcast.description: Copies the lane `s0` to every lane ($0 \le s0 < N$, with $N$ the number of lanes of the LMUL group; other values are undefined behavior).

bcast_b128.description: Copies the lane `s0` of each block of 128 bits to the lanes of the block ($0 \le s0 < B$, with $B$ the number of lanes of a block).

cabs.description: Modulus of the complex numbers (interleaved layout), in both lanes of each pair, without intermediate overflow: computed as $m \sqrt{(a_r/m)^2 + (a_i/m)^2}$ with $m$ the largest absolute value of the two parts.

cast.description: In-register bitcast/reinterpretation of a vector register to another datatype of identical bitwidth with zero runtime instructions.

cast_k.description: In-register bitcast/reinterpretation of a mask register to another datatype of identical bitwidth with zero runtime instructions.

cdiv.description: Complex division of the complex numbers of `vd0` by the ones of `vd1` (interleaved layout), with the algorithm of Smith: the division by the part of the largest absolute value avoids the overflows and the losses of $b_r^2 + b_i^2$.
cdiv.latex: \frac{a}{b} = \frac{(a_r b_r + a_i b_i) + i (a_i b_r - a_r b_i)}{b_r^2 + b_i^2}

cfmadd.description: Complex fused multiply-add: `vd0` * `vd1` + `vd2`, with complex numbers in the interleaved layout.

clamp.description: Clamps each element between the elements of the same lane of the second (lower bound) and third (upper bound) registers: `min(max(vd0, vd1), vd2)`. With a lower bound greater than the upper bound, the result is the upper bound. The form `vss` takes scalar bounds: `clamp(vd0, s0, s1)`.

cmpeq.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for equality ($a = b$). False when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmpge.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for greater-than-or-equal ($a \ge b$). False when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmpgt.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for greater-than ($a > b$). False when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmple.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for less-than-or-equal ($a \le b$). False when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmplt.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for less-than ($a < b$). False when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmpneq.description: Compares two vector registers element-wise for inequality ($a \ne b$). True when one of the two elements is NaN.

cmul.description: Complex product of the complex numbers (re, im) of the pairs of lanes of the two registers (interleaved layout: the real part in the even lane, the imaginary part in the odd lane).
cmul.latex: (a_r + i a_i)(b_r + i b_i) = (a_r b_r - a_i b_i) + i (a_r b_i + a_i b_r)

cmulconj.description: Complex product of the complex numbers of `vd0` by the conjugates of the complex numbers of `vd1` (interleaved layout).
cmulconj.latex: a \bar{b} = (a_r b_r + a_i b_i) + i (a_i b_r - a_r b_i)

cnorm.description: Squared modulus of the complex numbers (interleaved layout), in both lanes of each pair.

combine.description: Joins two vector registers into a register of the LMUL above (`d2` to `m1`, `m1` to `m2`, ...): the first one gives the lower half, the second one the upper half.
combine.latex: \text{res}_i = \begin{cases} vd0_i & \text{if } i < N \\ vd1_{i - N} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \quad 0 \le i < 2N

combine_k.description: Joins two mask registers into a mask of the LMUL above (`d2` to `m1`, `m1` to `m2`, ...): the first one gives the lower half, the second one the upper half.
combine_k.latex: m_{\text{res}, i} = \begin{cases} m_{0, i} & \text{if } i < N \\ m_{1, i - N} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \quad 0 \le i < 2N

compress.description: The active lanes of `vd0` (mask `vm0`), in order, packed at the beginning of the register; the other lanes are zero.

storeu_compress.description: Stores the active lanes of `vd0` (mask `vm0`), in order, at `p0` (no alignment required) and returns their number. Exactly this number of elements is written.

storeuf_compress.description: `storeu_compress` that may write a whole register: the active lanes of `vd0` at `p0`, then up to $N - c$ unspecified elements, with $c$ the number of active lanes (the memory of $N$ elements from `p0` must be writable). Faster than `storeu_compress` without a native masked store: a filter loop overwrites the unspecified elements with the next call (keep $N$ elements of margin at the end of the output).

conj.description: Complex conjugate: the imaginary parts (odd lanes) negated (interleaved layout).

copysign.description: Builds each element with the magnitude of the first register and the sign of the second one (IEEE copysign).

cos.description: Computes the trigonometric cosine of each floating-point element in radians.

cosh.description: Computes the hyperbolic cosine of each floating-point element.

count.description: Number of active lanes of a mask register.

cvt.description: Converts elements of a vector register to another datatype with numerical casting. A floating-point element converted to an integer is truncated toward zero, as a C cast: `2.7` gives `2` (call `round` first to round to the nearest integer). An integer without an exact floating-point representation is rounded to the nearest one. The conversion to an integer of a NaN, or of a value out of the range of the destination, gives a result that depends on the target.

unzip.description: Separates the even and the odd lanes: the even lanes in the lower half, the odd lanes in the upper half (interleaved to planar layout).

div.description: Divides the first vector register by the second element-wise.

div2.description: Divides each element of a vector register by 2 (via arithmetic shift for integers or multiplication/division for floats). For the negative integers the shift rounds toward $-\infty$, where the C division rounds toward zero: `-7` gives `-4`, not `-3`.

div4.description: Divides each element of a vector register by 4 (via arithmetic shift for integers or multiplication/division for floats). For the negative integers the shift rounds toward $-\infty$, where the C division rounds toward zero: `-7` gives `-2`, not `-1`.

dupeven.description: Copies each even lane to the next odd lane: lanes $2k$ and $2k+1$ both receive the lane $2k$.

dupodd.description: Copies each odd lane to the previous even lane: lanes $2k$ and $2k+1$ both receive the lane $2k+1$. A register of a single lane is unchanged.

exp.description: Computes the base-e exponential of each floating-point element.

expand.description: The inverse of `compress`: the first lanes of `vd0`, in order, go to the active lanes (mask `vm0`); the inactive lanes are zero.

loadu_expand.description: Loads as many elements from `p0` (no alignment required) as there are active lanes (mask `vm0`) and puts them in the active lanes, in order; the inactive lanes are zero. Only these elements are read.

fmadd.description: Computes the fused multiply-add of three vector registers ($a \times b + c$). The operation is fused (a single rounding) on the targets that have the instruction. Without it (SSE and AVX without FMA, and the scalar target depending on the compiler) the product is rounded before the addition, and the last bits of the result can differ.

fmsub.description: Computes the fused multiply-subtract of three vector registers ($a \times b - c$). The operation is fused (a single rounding) on the targets that have the instruction. Without it (SSE and AVX without FMA, and the scalar target depending on the compiler) the product is rounded before the addition, and the last bits of the result can differ.

fnmadd.description: Computes the fused negative multiply-add of three vector registers ($-(a \times b) + c$). The operation is fused (a single rounding) on the targets that have the instruction. Without it (SSE and AVX without FMA, and the scalar target depending on the compiler) the product is rounded before the addition, and the last bits of the result can differ.

fnmsub.description: Computes the fused negative multiply-subtract of three vector registers ($-(a \times b) - c$). The operation is fused (a single rounding) on the targets that have the instruction. Without it (SSE and AVX without FMA, and the scalar target depending on the compiler) the product is rounded before the addition, and the last bits of the result can differ.

gather.description: Loads elements from non-contiguous memory locations into a vector register using an index vector (unsigned indices counted in elements, of the width of the data or 32/64-bit: then at their own LMUL; 32-bit indices lower than $2^{31}$, and than $2^{30}$ on RVV for 32-bit data).

get.description: Extracts a single scalar element at index `s0` from a vector register.

get_k.description: Extracts the boolean truthiness of a single mask element at index `s0`.

getfirst.description: Extracts the first scalar element (element 0) from a vector register with minimal latency.

hadd.description: Computes the horizontal addition (reduction sum) of all elements in a vector register. For the floating-point types, the order of the additions depends on the target: the last bits of the result can differ from one target to another, and from a sequential sum.

hadds.description: Computes the horizontal addition with saturation of all elements in a vector register.

hi.description: Returns the upper half of a vector register as a register of the LMUL below (`m2` to `m1`, `m1` to `d2`, ...).

hi_k.description: Returns the upper half of a mask register as a mask of the LMUL below (`m2` to `m1`, `m1` to `d2`, ...).
hi_k.latex: m_{\text{res}, i} = m_{0, i + N/2}, \quad 0 \le i < N / 2

hmax.description: Computes the horizontal maximum (reduction maximum) of all elements in a vector register. With a NaN element, the result depends on the target.

hmin.description: Computes the horizontal minimum (reduction minimum) of all elements in a vector register. With a NaN element, the result depends on the target.

hmul.description: Computes the horizontal multiplication (reduction product) of all elements in a vector register. For the floating-point types, the order of the multiplications depends on the target: the last bits of the result can differ from one target to another, and from a sequential product.

zip.description: Interleaves the two halves of the register: the lane $2k$ receives the lane $k$, the lane $2k+1$ the lane $N/2 + k$ (planar to interleaved layout; the inverse of `unzip`).

load.description: Loads elements from an aligned memory address into a vector register.

loadu_unzip.description: Loads $N$ elements (no alignment required) and separates the even and the odd ones: the even elements in the lower half of the register, the odd ones in the upper half (`unzip(loadu(p0))`; with LMUL 2, the two LMUL 1 halves are the even and the odd elements of $2N$ elements, as ARM `vld2`).

loadu.description: Loads elements from an unaligned memory address into a vector register.

log.description: Computes the natural (base-e) logarithm of each floating-point element.

lo.description: Returns the lower half of a vector register as a register of the LMUL below (`m2` to `m1`, `m1` to `d2`, ...).

lo_k.description: Returns the lower half of a mask register as a mask of the LMUL below (`m2` to `m1`, `m1` to `d2`, ...).
lo_k.latex: m_{\text{res}, i} = m_{0, i}, \quad 0 \le i < N / 2

lshift.description: Shifts each element left by the number of bits of the same lane of the second register (from 0 to the number of bits of the type minus 1; any other count is undefined behavior). The shift by the same count for every lane is `lshift_vs` (`mipp::lshift(vd0, s0)` in C++).

lshift_vs.description: Shifts every element left by the same number of bits `s0` (scalar form `vs` of `lshift`; `mipp::lshift(vd0, s0)` in C++). The bits of the floating-point elements are shifted as an integer of the same size.

max.description: Selects the maximum value element-wise between two vector registers. When an element is NaN, the result depends on the target (the NaN or the other element), and so does the sign of the zero returned for `-0.0` and `0.0`.

min.description: Selects the minimum value element-wise between two vector registers. When an element is NaN, the result depends on the target (the NaN or the other element), and so does the sign of the zero returned for `-0.0` and `0.0`.

msb.description: Masks out all bits except the most significant bit (sign bit) for each vector element.

mul.description: Multiplies two vector registers element-wise. The integer multiplications keep the low bits of the product (modulo $2^n$).

ncvt.description: Narrowing conversion: converts vector elements to a narrower datatype, keeping the lanes in a register one LMUL below. The value is truncated (modulo for integers), not saturated.

ncvts.description: Converts each integer element to the type twice as narrow with saturation to its range; the result has the next LMUL down.

neg.description: Negates each element of a vector register. The most negative integer has no positive counterpart: its negation is itself (`-128` in `int8`).

none.description: Tests if every element in a mask register is zero (returns 1 if all inactive, 0 otherwise).

notb.description: Computes the bitwise NOT (inversion) of a vector register.

notb_k.description: Computes the bitwise NOT (inversion) of a mask register.

orb.description: Computes the bitwise OR of two vector registers.

orb_k.description: Computes the bitwise OR of two mask registers.
orb_k.latex: m_{\text{res}, i} = m_{0, i} \mid m_{1, i}

permute.description: Lane $i$ receives the lane `vd1[i]` of `vd0` (`vd1`: unsigned indices of the width of the elements, each below $N$, the number of lanes of the LMUL group; other values are undefined behavior).

permute2.description: Lane i receives the lane `vd2[i]` of the concatenation of `vd0` and `vd1` (indices below 2N; other values are undefined behavior).

permute_b128.description: `permute` in each block of 128 bits: lane $i$ receives the lane `vd1[i]` of its block (indices below the number of lanes of a block; x86 `vpermilps`, `pshufb`).

pow.description: Computes the first vector register raised to the power of the second element-wise.

pow2.description: Computes 2 raised to the power of each vector element.

reverse.description: Reverses the order of the lanes of the register (of the whole LMUL group).

reverse_b128.description: Reverses the order of the lanes in each block of 128 bits (the whole register when it is smaller).

rotate.description: Rotates the lanes down by `s0` ($0 \le s0 < N$): the lane $i$ receives the lane $(i + s0) \bmod N$.

rotate_b128.description: `rotate` in each block of 128 bits ($0 \le s0 < B$, with $B$ the number of lanes of a block).

round.description: Rounds each floating-point element to the nearest integer. A tie is rounded away from zero, as the C function `round`: `2.5` gives `3` and `-2.5` gives `-3`.

rshift.description: Shifts each element right by the number of bits of the same lane of the second register: arithmetic shift (copies of the sign bit) for the signed types, logical shift (zeros) for the unsigned ones. Counts from 0 to the number of bits of the type minus 1; any other count is undefined behavior. The shift by the same count for every lane is `rshift_vs` (`mipp::rshift(vd0, s0)` in C++), and the logical shift of the signed types is `rshiftl`.

rshift_vs.description: Shifts every element right by the same number of bits `s0` (scalar form `vs` of `rshift`; `mipp::rshift(vd0, s0)` in C++): arithmetic shift for the signed types, logical shift for the unsigned ones. The bits of the floating-point elements are shifted as an unsigned integer of the same size. The logical shift of the signed types is `rshiftl_vs`.

rshiftl.description: Shifts each element right by the number of bits of the same lane of the second register, with a logical shift (zeros enter on the left) for all the types: the signed elements are shifted as the unsigned integer of the same size, like `(int32_t)((uint32_t)a >> n)` in C. Same result as `rshift` on the unsigned types. Counts from 0 to the number of bits of the type minus 1; any other count is undefined behavior. The shift by the same count for every lane is `rshiftl_vs` (`mipp::rshiftl(vd0, s0)` in C++).

rshiftl_vs.description: Shifts every element right by the same number of bits `s0` (scalar form `vs` of `rshiftl`; `mipp::rshiftl(vd0, s0)` in C++), with a logical shift (zeros enter on the left) for all the types: the signed and floating-point elements are shifted as the unsigned integer of the same size. Same result as `rshift_vs` on the unsigned and floating-point types.

rsqrt.description: Computes an estimate of the reciprocal square root of each floating-point element ($1 / \sqrt{a}$). Its precision is the one of the instruction of the target: from two or three significant digits (the estimates of NEON and RVV) to the exact value. Divide by `sqrt` when the last digits matter.

scatter.description: Stores vector elements into non-contiguous memory locations using an index vector (unsigned indices counted in elements, of the width of the data or 32/64-bit: then at their own LMUL; 32-bit indices lower than $2^{31}$, and than $2^{30}$ on RVV for 32-bit data).

select.description: Selects elements between two vector registers based on a mask (`vd0` in the active lanes of `vm0`, `vd1` in the others).

set.description: Initializes a vector register from a scalar array.

set0.description: Initializes a vector register with all zeros.

set0_k.description: Clears all elements of a mask register (all inactive).

set1.description: Broadcasts a single scalar value to all elements of a vector register.

set1_k.description: Broadcasts boolean truthiness to all elements of a mask register.

set_k.description: Initializes a mask register from an array of `int32_t` evaluating boolean truthiness.

signbit.description: Returns the mask of the elements whose sign bit is set (negative values, including -0.0 for the floating-point types).

sin.description: Computes the trigonometric sine of each floating-point element in radians.

sinh.description: Computes the hyperbolic sine of each floating-point element.

slide.description: Window of $N$ lanes at the position `s0` ($0 \le s0 \le N$) of the concatenation of the two registers: the lanes $s0$ to $N-1$ of `vd0`, then the lanes $0$ to $s0-1$ of `vd1` (x86 `alignr`, ARM `ext`).

slide_b128.description: `slide` in each block of 128 bits: the window at `s0` of the concatenation of the blocks of `vd0` and `vd1` ($0 \le s0 \le B$, with $B$ the number of lanes of a block; x86 `alignr`).

slidedown.description: Moves the lanes down by `s0` ($0 \le s0 \le N$): the lane $i$ receives the lane $i + s0$, the lanes from $N - s0$ are zero.

slidedown_b128.description: `slidedown` in each block of 128 bits, zeros entering at the top of each block (x86 `psrldq`).

slideup.description: Moves the lanes up by `s0` ($0 \le s0 \le N$): the lane $i$ receives the lane $i - s0$, the lanes below $s0$ are zero.

slideup_b128.description: `slideup` in each block of 128 bits, zeros entering at the bottom of each block (x86 `pslldq`).

sqrt.description: Computes the square root of each element in a vector register.

store.description: Stores vector elements into an aligned memory address.

storeu_zip.description: Interleaves the two halves of the register and stores the $N$ elements (no alignment required): `storeu(p0, zip(vd0))`, the inverse of `loadu_unzip` (ARM `vst2`).

storeu.description: Stores vector elements into an unaligned memory address.

sub.description: Subtracts the second vector register from the first element-wise. The integer subtractions wrap around (modulo $2^n$); `subs` saturates instead.

subs.description: Subtracts two integer vector registers element-wise with saturation to [MIN, MAX] on underflow/overflow.

swap2.description: Swaps the lanes of each pair (lanes $2k$ and $2k+1$). A register of a single lane is unchanged.

tan.description: Computes the trigonometric tangent of each floating-point element in radians.

tanh.description: Computes the hyperbolic tangent of each floating-point element.

testz.description: Tests if the bitwise AND of two mask registers is all zero (returns 1 if disjoint/all zero, 0 otherwise).

tovd.description: Expands a mask register into an all-ones (`~0`) / all-zeros (`0`) vector register.

tovm.description: Converts vector elements to mask elements: a lane is active when its element has at least one non-zero bit (so `-0.0` is active), and the resulting mask lane has all its bits set.

trunc.description: Truncates each floating-point element toward zero.

unziplo.description: Even lanes of the concatenation of the two registers: `vd0[0]`, `vd0[2]`... then `vd1[0]`, `vd1[2]`... (with `lo` / `hi`, the even lanes of a register of twice the LMUL; ARM `uzp1`).

unziplo_b128.description: `unziplo` in each block of 128 bits (x86 `shufps` with the even lanes).

unziphi.description: Odd lanes of the concatenation of the two registers: `vd0[1]`, `vd0[3]`... then `vd1[1]`, `vd1[3]`... (ARM `uzp2`).

wcvt.description: Widening conversion: converts vector elements to a wider datatype.

xorb.description: Computes the bitwise XOR of two vector registers.

xorb_k.description: Computes the bitwise XOR of two mask registers.
xorb_k.latex: m_{\text{res}, i} = m_{0, i} \oplus m_{1, i}

xorsign.description: Negates each element of the first register where the element of the second register is negative (sign bit set).

ziphi.description: Interleaves the lanes of the upper halves of the two registers: `vd0[N/2]`, `vd1[N/2]`, `vd0[N/2+1]`... (the second half of `zip`).

ziphi_b128.description: `ziphi` in each block of 128 bits: interleaves the lanes of the upper halves of the blocks (x86 `unpackhi`).

ziplo.description: Interleaves the lanes of the lower halves of the two registers: `vd0[0]`, `vd1[0]`, `vd0[1]`, `vd1[1]`... (the first half of `zip`).

ziplo_b128.description: `ziplo` in each block of 128 bits: interleaves the lanes of the lower halves of the blocks (x86 `unpacklo`).
